maria: Ran a focused nsys + heap profile during the KV-cache regression window — attaching a quick writeup.

maria: tl;dr: periodic cudaMalloc spikes (~8–18ms) every ~25s. nvtx shows these line up with kernel-selection handoffs when batcher upsizes batches (8->16). suspect arena churn + small-slab scavenging. :thinking_face:

maria: command used: ```nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=/tmp/run1998881234.qdrep ./bin/runtime --cfg configs/kv_bench.yaml```

perf-bot: capture saved: s3://perf-artifacts/eng-runtime/1998881234/run1998881234.qdrep :white_check_mark:

ankit: nice. do you have the host-side callstack around the mallocs? is it cudaMalloc or cudaMallocAsync?

maria: snapshot of nvtx timeline: ```
[20.1s] select_kernel_v3() start -> batcher->scale_up
[20.12s] kv_cache_prefetch
[20.13s] cudaMemAlloc(32KB)  <-- 12.3ms
[20.14s] launch kernel: attention_forward_qk
[20.15s] kernel schedule delay ~4ms
[45.2s] repeat pattern
```

jess: those 32KB allocs smell like KV slab allocations that fail fast and fall back to arena. Could be fragmentation causing repeated slow cudaMallocs.

sam: Did you collect a heap-snapshot with our cuda-pool debug flags? ``--cuda-pool-sample=on --pool-snapshot=/tmp/pool.json``

maria: Yep, ran pool snapshot. Key observations in /tmp/pool199888.json (paste): ``free_chunks_by_size: {32KB: 3, 64KB: 0, 128KB: 1}, arena_live: 1.2GB, slab_alloc_rate: bursty at ~600ops/s``

ekaterina: If free 64KB is 0 but 32KB is small, small-request splitting could trigger fallback to slow cudaMalloc when no perfect-fit slab. Any split policy logs?

maria: split_policy = "try_fit_then_reuse" in this capture. The allocator does a best-effort coalesce but we see many tiny external fragments due to heterogeneous lifetime of KV entries.

ankit: Another angle: kernel selection upsizing means bigger KV cache entries for later layers -> transient increase in working set and eviction. Eviction path may do cudaMalloc to copy out or compact. Check eviction NVTX markers.

maria: eviction markers present: ``evict_range(start=0x7f..., bytes=64KB)`` immediately before cudaMalloc. timeline suggests eviction tries to allocate temp buffer and that path uses cudaMalloc (not pool).

jess: that's the root. Eviction should use pool-backed temporary buffers. Why is it falling back? maybe a bug in the pool's 'allow_external' gate when under batcher-change codepath.

sam: I replayed with env var: ``REDWOOD_CUDA_POOL_DEBUG=1 REDWOOD_CUDA_POOL_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=0``. With that, the runtime logs: ``pool_alloc(size=64KB) -> no-fit -> triggered_compact -> compacted 128KB -> pool still no-fit -> fail -> record fallback_to_cudaMalloc``. So compact doesn't free the exact power-of-two required.

ekaterina: Possible fixes: 1) enhance compaction to merge adjacent free runs across slab boundaries; 2) add transient staging buffers in host pinned memory instead of immediate device cudaMalloc; 3) make kernel-selection path pre-reserve pool capacity when upsizing batcher.

maria: I also ran nsys kernel timeline with timestamps overlayed. The ordering shows: select_kernel_v3 -> pool_compact -> cudaMalloc -> kernel_launch. The cudaMalloc latency pushes kernel launch later (3–6ms) and shifts subsequent kernels causing increased latency tail.

ankit: For a quick mitigation, can we change select_kernel to pre-allocate expected additional KV footprint before switching? e.g., call pool_reserve(batch_delta) and fall back to deferring upsizes when reserve fails.

jess: that seems low-risk. Also add a metric: pool_fallback_count per route so we can correlate with user latencies.

maria: agreed. I'll prototype a patch that does pre-reserve and add a nvtx marker around reserve calls. will re-run capture.

perf-bot: TODO created: PERF-3247 add pre-reserve to kernel selection + metric pool_fallback_count (assignee: maria)

sam: Can you also attach the nsys slice with kernel timestamps (for perf review)? I want to annotate delays on the perf board.

maria: uploaded: https://perfboard.internal/nsys/1998881234/timeline.png :eyes:

ankit: small follow-up: check if cudaMallocAsync is enabled on those hosts. If driver/kernel mismatch, async may degrade to sync cudaMalloc behavior.

maria: good call — driver is 525.85, cuda runtime 11.8, cudaMallocAsync supported but in our builds the pool is used. I saw occasional fallback because pool lock contention timed out, not purely fragmentation. Need to measure pool lock wait times.

ekaterina: capture suggestion for next run: enable `--trace=mutex` and increase nsys sampling window to include a full 2-minute run to capture multiple churn events.

maria: will do. next steps: (1) prototype pre-reserve in kernel-selector, (2) instrument pool to refuse fallback and emit metric, (3) run extended nsys with mutex tracing. Will report back Monday.

ankit: thanks — big win if we can avoid the sync cudaMallocs. :thumbsup:
